Woodside Energy Expects Elevated LNG Pricing in 4Q — Interview

SYDNEY--Woodside Energy expects its liquefied natural gas will continue to fetch elevated prices into the year end as customers vie to secure enough supply for the northern hemisphere winter in a tight global market.

Woodside on Wednesday said it achieved a realized LNG price of $84 per barrel of oil equivalent in the three months through September. That was up 27% on the prior quarter and contributed to operating revenue of $4.28 billion.

Woodside attributed the improvement to the realization of LNG price lags from the second quarter and stronger gas hub market pricing. Around 33% of LNG sold by Woodside in the third quarter was linked to gas hub indices.
"With the lag in pricing we'll continue to see some elevated pricing through the year," Chief Executive Liz Westcott said in an interview.

Iranian attacks on Qatar have damaged key infrastructure producing LNG for export and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has limited energy flows through the Persian Gulf. At the same time, European nations have sought to wean themselves off LNG supply from Russia due to the war in Ukraine.
The result is higher prices and the heightened appeal of LNG from sources that bypass the Middle East, including from the U.S. and Australia.

Woodside aims to lean into that demand by bringing on the Scarborough Energy Project in Australia within the next couple of months. The company said the project remains on budget and on track to ship its maiden cargo of liquefied natural gas by the end of this year.
Its medium-term project pipeline includes the Louisiana LNG project in the U.S., which was 32% complete at the end of September. Woodside is seeking to produce LNG for the first time there in 2029.
